transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (CTO - HarborPulse), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect), Evan Cho (Security), Lena Brooks (DevOps)
Shared: private_connectivity_playbook_v1.pdf (link), redwood-security-pack.zip (to be sent)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Goal: understand HarborPulse network posture and constraints for Private deployment of Redwood (VPC peering / PrivateLink / Private Endpoints), requirements for egress IPs, data residency in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
- Key concerns: static egress IPs, transit gateway topology, SOC2/KMS, SAML SSO, firewall whitelisting, canary/fallback to hosted.
- Next: Redwood sends security pack + terraform samples; customer supplies VPC CIDRs and NAT IPs; schedule pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time. i'm Alex from Redwood, i'll run through objectives quick — want to make sure we understand your network layout and egress constraints so we can land a Private deployment for HarborPulse.
[00:15] Jordan (CTO): yeah thanks — we've been evaluating Redwood for model serving, main ask is private-only traffic, no internet egress from our VPC to public endpoints. also need predictable outbound IPs for firewall whitelist, multi-region in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 for latency.
[00:29] Priya (Cloud Architect): to add, we use TGW (transit gateway) between accounts, our Prod VPCs sit in a separate AWS account. ideally Redwood private endpoints land in a dedicated infra VPC and we peer or attach via TGW.
[00:42] Samir (SE): got it. two common approaches: PrivateLink-style endpoints per-region or dedicated Redwood Private deployed in your VPCs with peering/transit attachments. each has tradeoffs on IPs, routing, and management.
[00:57] Evan (Security): quick Q — do you support static egress IP blocks so our external partners can whitelist? we cannot open wide ranges.
[01:05] Maya (Solutions Eng): yes — for Private we can provide a set of egress IPs per-region (NAT or egress-proxy) or we can run in your account so you control NAT egress. if using Redwood-managed infra we provide an egress pool that we can guarantee per contract — subject to network ACLs and provider constraints.
[01:28] Jordan: and for data residency, some workloads must stay in eu-west-1, others us-east-1 — can we pin models to regions so the KV cache and token generation happen entirely in-region?
[01:38] Samir: absolutely — routing policy supports region pinning; you'll configure model routing rules so specific routes use eu-west-1 instances. for cross-region fallback we can default back to a secondary region but that's configurable.
[01:50] Lena (DevOps): are there issues with DNS? we use private hosted zones and need internal names, can we set up private endpoints with CNAMEs into our zone?
[01:59] Maya: yes; typical pattern is creating interface endpoints with private IPs and optional private DNS. if you want to control the CNAMES we can provide the FQDN and you create an alias in your private zone, or we can publish a private hosted zone delegation. note sometimes cross-account DNS needs additional resolver rules if using TGW.
[02:20] Priya: how about TLS termination and certs — we need mTLS to our side for call authenticity and KMS integration?
[02:28] Samir: we support mutual TLS for customer tunnels and also integrate with customer-managed KMS for key wrapping, especially in Private deployments. we'll capture the cert thumbprints during onboarding.
[02:39] Evan: SOC2 docs? audit logs? we need to know retention, access patterns, and how to prove model access didn't leak PII.
[02:47] Alex: we'll send SOC2 attestation and our audit-log export spec. for Private we push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders or s3 bucket with KMS. we'll include our retention defaults and how to configure longer retention if you need.
[03:01] Jordan: cool. question on IP planning — our prod VPC is 10.10.0.0/16, infra VPC is 10.20.0.0/16, do you require contiguous ranges or specific subnets for endpoints?
[03:10] Maya: we need interface endpoint ENIs in subnets that have available IPs; typical practice is to reserve /28 per AZ for private endpoints. for peering we only need non-overlapping CIDRs; if you're using TGW attachments we also need route table entries and propagate routes.
[03:28] Priya: we use AWS NAT Gateways in prod; if redwood-managed infra egresses via NAT, can you guarantee the egress IPs won't change month-to-month? our vendor whitelists are strict.
[03:39] Samir: if we provide managed egress we contractualize a set of static IPs for the duration of the commitment. if you self-host in your account then you control NATs and IPs. tradeoff: Redwood-managed gives less operational burden, self-host gives more IP control.
[03:55] Jordan: what's the recommended pattern if we want least blast radius but easy upgrades?
[04:01] Maya: recommended is hybrid: Redwood deploys private infrastructure in your VPC (or connected infra VPC) and we do canary routing — a canary subnet and policies that allow staged rollouts. if you want to avoid touching prod VPCs we can attach to your infra VPC via TGW and use routing to control which subnets talk to Redwood endpoints.
[04:20] Lena: any port requirements for firewall?
[04:23] Samir: mostly HTTPS 443 for API traffic; for metrics/tracing we might need outbound 443 to hosted telemetry endpoints unless you opt for pulling logs via s3. if you want eBPF or agent-based telemetry, that could open additional ports but it's optional.
[04:39] Evan: what about peering throughput / cross-az charges — are there cost impacts we should budget for when traffic goes through TGW?
[04:46] Maya: yes TGW data transfer costs apply; also cross-AZ traffic fees if endpoints live in different AZs. we can provide a cost estimate model based on expected tokens per second and payload sizes.
[05:00] Jordan: curious about failure modes — if your region runs out of capacity what is fallback?
[05:06] Samir: we have model-variant fallbacks and regional routing fallbacks. policies can automatically route to a compatible quantized model in another region, or degrade to hosted with observability alerts. for mission-critical, we recommend reserved capacity (Dedicated) with SLA.
[05:22] Priya: timeline — how long to get from kickoff to pilot?
[05:26] Alex: typical pilot is 1-2 weeks for basic private endpoints and a small test workload, assuming network info is provided quickly. full production is 4-8 weeks depending on cross-account networking and compliance work.
[05:40] Jordan: ok that works. we have some external partners that call into our IP allowlist; we need static egress IPs for Redwood to present to them. can you give a sample CIDR size?
[05:50] Samir: we normally provide a /28 or set of fixed IPs per-region for egress; if you need fewer we can island them into a static NAT or egress proxy. we'll include sample terraform for the NAT egress or a managed egress pool config.
[06:05] Priya: any constraints for PrivateLink and multi-region? PrivateLink endpoints are regional — we'd need a design for routing between regions via TGW if model traffic must be multi-region.
[06:16] Maya: correct, PrivateLink is regional. if you need active-active multi-region, the recommended pattern is per-region endpoints and a traffic-router (client-side or infra-side) to choose region. TGW will carry cross-region traffic but be mindful of costs and latency.
[06:34] Jordan: what about AWS GovCloud / restricted regions? we have one workload that might have to run in a regulated cloud.
[06:41] Alex: we support Private deployments in customer-managed on-prem or air-gapped via our Private product — that requires additional legal and infra setup. for region-gated clouds we can discuss a custom plan — usually longer lead time.
[06:55] Evan: SSO — we use Okta with SAML. how does admin access work for Redwood console for on-prem/private?
[07:03] Samir: single sign-on is supported; for Private we can run a control plane that integrates with your Okta via SAML; RBAC maps groups to roles. we'll capture the SAML metadata during onboarding.
[07:16] Priya: any ephemeral KV cache concerns? tokens cached in memory — do they ever leave the region if a node is terminated and failover happens?
[07:26] Samir: KV cache is local to the serving cluster; with region pinning we keep it in-region. if you enable cross-region fallback that cache won't replicate automatically — it's part of the design tradeoff. we'll document consistency expectations.
[07:44] Lena: curious about testing — for pilot we want to validate latency and egress IPs. what does Redwood need from us to run an e2e smoke test?
[07:53] Maya: share VPC CIDRs, security group rules, a test namespace and the IPs of systems that will call Redwood. we can spin up test endpoints and provide curl examples that present the egress ip so you can confirm whitelisting.
[08:10] Jordan: any limit on connections or concurrency for private endpoints?
[08:14] Samir: depends on the infra sizing; for pilot we'll use a small footprint with burstable TPS. production Dedicated gets reserved throughput. we'll propose recommended concurrency and token/sec numbers once we see expected qps.
[08:29] Alex: okay recap and immediate asks — Redwood will send the security pack (SOC2, architecture, network checklist), sample terraform for endpoints/NAT, and a short runbook for canary failover. HarborPulse to share VPC CIDRs, TGW details, NAT IPs and target test list. schedule pilot kickoff for week of 7/13.
[08:50] Jordan: sounds good. any blockers from your side to provide the egress IPs in contract?
[08:55] Alex: none, we'll include egress commitments in the SOW and the IP list in the network appendix; if you need contract-level guarantees we'll loop legal after the pilot.
[09:06] Priya: oh, one more — we use ip allowlists with strict source port expectations for a legacy partner; can you ensure ephemeral source ports are preserved?
[09:16] Samir: source port preservation is tough through NATs — recommend whitelisting by source IP + TLS client cert. we can also run an egress proxy with client certs. we'll note this in the checklist.
[09:32] Evan: please also include how you rotate keys and how audit logs show model invocations.
[09:38] Maya: sure, we'll include rotation cadence, KMS integration options, and a sample audit export that maps request IDs to timestamps and user tokens.
[09:49] Alex: excellent — shall we agree on action items and the pilot date?
[09:53] Jordan: agree. 7/13 works for us, we'll confirm in email. thanks team.
[09:59] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by tomorrow with the pack.

End of transcript.
